content.key_idea: NaxRiscv's out-of-order pipeline buffers RTOSUnit custom instructions in a small in-order queue from decode through commit, flushing on misspeculation, so only correctly-speculated, in-order instructions reach the RTOSUnit.

summary: This figure shows how RTOSUnit's custom instructions are integrated into NaxRiscv, a fully out-of-order, speculative RISC-V core. The six-stage pipeline (F, D, I, X, W, C) boxes I, X, and W as the out-of-order region. Because custom instructions must execute strictly in program order and non-speculatively, an Instruction queue buffers them: the in-order decode stage D inserts a custom instruction (a), the issue stage I later adds its resolved arguments (b), a misspeculated instruction causes the queue to be flushed (c), and once the instruction reaches the commit stage C (d) it is passed with its arguments (e) to the RTOSUnit for execution. This small in-order buffer lets NaxRiscv keep issuing and executing other instructions out of order without stalling the pipeline for the RTOSUnit's instructions to resolve.
summary_zh: 该图展示 RTOSUnit 自定义指令在乱序核 NaxRiscv 中的整合：译码阶段 D 将指令送入指令队列，发射阶段 I 补充参数，误预测则清空队列，提交阶段 C 确认后才把指令连同参数传给 RTOSUnit 执行。
